A man in his 40s presented with a 3-month history of an asymptomatic nodule on his scalp. No systemic complaints, history of arthropod bite, immunosuppression, travel abroad, or contact with animals in the recent past.
Physical examination revealed a skin-colored, firm, nontender, freely mobile 2 × 1.5-cm nodule with overlying normal skin on the right occipital region of the scalp. There was no lymphadenopathy. No other cutaneous lesions were present.
